steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on SINGLE, a method that models users' constant and instant article viewing flows with large language models for article recommendation. Cover the motivation, related news recommendation work, the method, and the offline and online results.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. Motivation: online article platforms and information overload
2. Existing news recommendation models and their limits
3. Our method: SINGLE (constant and instant viewing flows)
4. Experiments, online deployment and findings

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Motivation
- platforms: Microsoft News, Zhihu, CSDN, Blog -> visit news, exchange ideas, learn professional knowledge
- information overload -> users lose patience finding what they need among massive articles
- article recommendation system needed to satisfy information needs
- most article rec models focus on news recommendation: learn interest from previously clicked news, return related news

2. Existing news recommendation models
- focus on personalized news recommendation techniques
- candidate news may contain multiple aspects, topics, entities; need accurate matching with user interest
- learn article representations from text (titles, bodies); personalized attention to reweight tokens
- clicked-news sequence contains noise for representing user interest
- so lots of work adds user personalized info: user IDs, user context information, user feedback
- LLMs (e.g. GPT3): strong ability to summarize user characteristics to match items with user interests

3. SINGLE (u S er view ING f L ow mod E ling)
- Figure 1: model constant and instant viewing flows -> general and instant user interests
- constant viewing flow: prompt the LLM as a user to extract user preferences and characteristics from visited articles
- instant viewing flow: learn different interest views
  - encode title + body with BERT
  - interactions between visited-article and candidate-article representations
  - attentively read visited articles -> user instant interest representation
- use text from titles and bodies to represent article semantics
  - summarization prompt with title as the gist
  - LLM extracts keywords from bodies, then generates a brief paragraph for the body

4. Experiments and findings
- datasets: MIND (news), Alibaba Technology Association (ATA) (technique articles) -> SINGLE effective
- deployed on the online website of Alibaba; 2.4% improvement in online A/B test
- analyses: mimics different article viewing behaviors, more effective recommendation system
- constant flow: learns general interests, user representations more similar to clicked articles
- instant flow: weights clicked articles differently according to the candidate article; captures consistent topic or topic shift

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
There are online platforms like Microsoft News, Zhihu, CSDN, and Blog, and they give users a chance to visit news information, exchange their ideas and also learn professional knowledge. But there is an overload of information, and users exhaust their patience trying to find the information they really need from the massive number of articles. So an article recommendation system is necessary to help users find related articles that satisfy their information needs. A lot of article recommendation models mainly focus on the news recommendation task, where the model learns the user interest from the news articles the user clicked before and returns related news articles for the user.

The existing news recommendation models pay more attention to personalized news recommendation techniques. In news recommendation, a candidate news article can contain multiple aspects, topics and entities, and the models need to match the candidate news with the user interest accurately. These models learn representations of news articles from textual information such as titles and bodies, and they design a personalized attention mechanism that reweights different tokens when learning the news article representations. Also, the sequence of news articles that the user clicked usually has some noise in it for representing the user's interest. Because of this, lots of work uses user personalized information to capture the user interest from the clicked articles better, for example user IDs, user context information and user feedback. Large Language Models (LLMs), for example GPT3, have shown strong abilities to summarize user characteristics so that items can be matched better with user interests.

3. SINGLE (u S er view ING f L ow mod E ling)
- Figure 1: model constant and instant viewing flows -> general and instant user interests
- constant flow: prompt the LLM as a user to extract preferences and characteristics from visited articles
- instant flow: BERT encodes title + body; interactions between visited and candidate articles; attentive reading -> instant interest representation
- article semantics from titles and bodies: summarization prompt with title as gist; LLM extracts keywords from bodies, then brief paragraph

4. Experiments and findings
- MIND (news) and Alibaba Technology Association (ATA) (technique articles) -> effective
- deployed on online website of Alibaba; 2.4% improvement in online A/B test
- analyses: mimics different viewing behaviors
- constant flow: general interests, user reps closer to clicked articles
- instant flow: weights clicked articles by candidate article; consistent topic or topic shift

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
There are online platforms like Microsoft News, Zhihu, CSDN, and Blog, and they give users a chance to visit news information, exchange their ideas and also learn professional knowledge. But there is an overload of information, and users exhaust their patience trying to find the information they really need from the massive number of articles. So an article recommendation system is necessary to help users find related articles that satisfy their information needs. A lot of article recommendation models mainly focus on the news recommendation task, where the model learns the user interest from the news articles the user clicked before and returns related news articles for the user.

The existing news recommendation models pay more attention to personalized news recommendation techniques. In news recommendation, a candidate news article can contain multiple aspects, topics and entities, and the models need to match the candidate news with the user interest accurately. These models learn representations of news articles from textual information such as titles and bodies, and they design a personalized attention mechanism that reweights different tokens when learning the news article representations. Also, the sequence of news articles that the user clicked usually has some noise in it for representing the user's interest. Because of this, lots of work uses user personalized information to capture the user interest from the clicked articles better, for example user IDs, user context information and user feedback. Large Language Models (LLMs), for example GPT3, have shown strong abilities to summarize user characteristics so that items can be matched better with user interests.

In this paper we propose a method called u S er view ING f L ow mod E ling (SINGLE) to recommend articles to users. As Figure 1 shows, we model the constant viewing flow and the instant viewing flow to represent the interest of users better, and this helps extract the general and the instant user interests for recommendation. To be specific, we model the constant viewing flow by prompting the LLM as a user so it extracts the user preferences and characteristics from the visited articles. Then SINGLE models the instant viewing flow to learn the different interest views of users. It encodes the title and body of an article with BERT, it builds interactions between the representations of user-visited articles and candidate articles, and it attentively reads the representations of the visited articles to get the user instant interest representation. SINGLE also uses the text information from the titles and bodies of the articles to represent the article semantics better. For this we design a summarization prompt that uses the article title as the gist, we use LLMs to extract keywords from the article bodies, and then we generate a brief paragraph that represents the article body.

We run experiments on the news recommendation dataset MIND and on the technique article recommendation dataset Alibaba Technology Association (ATA), and the results show that SINGLE is effective. We also deploy the SINGLE model on the online website of Alibaba. SINGLE gets 2.4% improvements in the online A/B test, which is strong evidence of its advantages in article recommendation tasks. Our further analyses show the SINGLE model can mimic different article viewing behaviors and build a more effective article recommendation system. The user constant viewing flow modeling method learns general user interests and makes the user representations more similar to the clicked articles. Then the user instant viewing flow gives different weights to the user-clicked articles depending on the candidate article, and in this way it captures the different user interests from the visited articles. It can capture a consistent topic or a topic shift in the clicked article sequence.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Online platforms, such as Microsoft News, Zhihu, CSDN, and Blog, give users an opportunity to visit news information, exchange ideas and learn professional knowledge [1,2]. However, the overload of information makes users exhaust their patience when finding the really needed information from massive articles. They learn the representations of news articles from textual information, such as titles and bodies, and design a personalized attention mechanism to reweight different tokens when learning the news article representations [17]. On the other hand, the sequence of user-clicked news articles usually contains some noise for representing the user's interest. Thus, lots of work considers user personalized information to better capture user interest from the clicked articles, such as user IDs [17,3], user context information [18,19] and user feedback [20,15]. Large Language Models (LLMs), such as GPT3 [21], have shown strong abilities in summarizing user characteristics to better match items with user interests [22,23,24,25].

In this paper, we propose a u S er view ING f L ow mod E ling (SINGLE) method to recommend articles for users. As shown in Figure 1, we model the constant and instant viewing flows to better represent user interest, which helps to extract the general and instant user interests for recommendation. Specifically, we model the constant viewing flow by prompting the LLM as a user to extract user preferences and characteristics from visited articles. Then SINGLE models the instant viewing flow to learn different interest views of users.
